distinctness.vs_H_1482_binocular_rivalry: RIVALRY = on a FIXED (constant) input, dominance SPONTANEOUSLY alternates over time (adaptation fatigues the winner -> A->B->A); its alternation statistics are INVARIANT to the order in which a stimulus is presented (no swept control parameter, time/fatigue driven). HYSTERESIS = on a CHANGING input, the perceptual switch-point DEPENDS on the input HISTORY (which direction it was approached from); NO spontaneous alternation on a held input (input-history driven). Bar B contrasts the two on the IDENTICAL ascending vs descending sweep: a rivalry-style readout (adaptation, NO evidence-history inertia) closes the loop (|area|=0.048, order-invariant) while hysteresis shifts the switch-point (0.327). Same competition, different DEPENDENCY: rivalry on TIME ⊥ hysteresis on input-HISTORY.
distinctness.vs_H_1465_habituation: HABITUATION = a REPEATED stimulus' response DECAYS (decreasing magnitude, stimulus-specific, recovers on a dishabituating event). HYSTERESIS is NOT a decay — the percept is STICKY (held in its prior state) and the lag is DIRECTION-dependent, not a monotone decline. Ablating the history-inertia term (bar D) removes the direction-dependence entirely (it is not a fading magnitude). distinct: habituation = magnitude decay over repeats ⊥ hysteresis = direction-dependent switch-point lag over a swept input.
